Surah al-Mursalat (The Emissaries) [Meccan; its verses are fifty]

﴿By those [winds] sent forth in succession﴾, i.e., the winds, consecutive like the mane of a horse, one following another; and its accusative (naṣb) is in the sense of a circumstantial state (ḥāl).
ﷻ﴿By the winds that blow with violence﴾ — the strong winds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 77, verse 3:

﴿By those [winds] that scatter [the rain] in spreading﴾ — the winds scatter the rain.
﴿By those that separate, separating﴾, meaning: the verses of the Qur'an separate between truth and falsehood, and between the lawful and the unlawful.
﴿Then by those who convey the reminder﴾: that is, the angels who descend with the revelation to the prophets and messengers, and who convey the revelation to the nations.

﴿As an excuse or a warning﴾, i.e., for the giving of excuse and warning from God Most High. And in one recitation (qira'a), the dhal of نُذْرًا is vocalized with a damma, and it was also recited with a damma on the dhal of عُذْرًا.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 77, verse 7:

﴿Indeed, what you are promised﴾ i.e., O disbelievers of Makkah, of resurrection and punishment, ﴿is surely going to occur﴾, existing without doubt.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 77, verse 8:

﴿Then when the stars are obliterated﴾ their light is erased.
﴿And when the heaven is opened﴾ is split apart.
﴿And when the mountains are blown away﴾, they are crushed to dust and set in motion.

﴿And when the messengers are assembled at their appointed time﴾. The word أُقِّتَتْ (uqqitat) is read with a waw (و) and, in place of it, with a hamza (glottal stop), meaning that they are gathered for a set time.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 77, verse 12:

﴿For what Day﴾ [it has been] postponed, for a great Day. ﴿Were they postponed?﴾ for the testimony against their nations concerning the conveying [of the message].

Tafsir al-Jalalayn commentary on Surah 77, verse 13:

﴿For the Day of Decision﴾, [the Day that separates] between the creatures; and from this is derived the answer to "when" (idhā), meaning: when the Decision occurs between the creatures.
"And what will make you know what the Day of Decision is?" — an emphatic expression to magnify its matter.

Woe on that day to the deniers! ﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾. This is a threat to them.

Wait, I need to correct that. Here is the faithful translation of the passage as given:

"Woe on that day to the deniers" (﴿ويل يومئذ للمكذبين﴾). This is a threat (wa'id) against them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 77, verse 16:

﴿Did We not destroy the former peoples?﴾ by their denial, i.e., We destroyed them.
Then We shall follow them up with the later ones (of those who denied), like the disbelievers of Makkah, so We shall destroy them.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 77 (al-Mursalat), verse 18:

﴿Thus﴾ like what We did to the deniers (al-mukadhdhibin) ﴿We shall do to the criminals﴾ with everyone who commits crime in the future, so We will destroy them.

Woe on that day to those who deny!

Commentary: "Repetition for emphasis" (ta'kid).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 77, verse 20:

﴿Did We not create you from a despised fluid?﴾ Weak, and it is the seminal fluid (al-maniyy).
﴿So We placed him in a secure resting-place﴾ — ḥarīz, meaning the womb.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 77, verse 22:

﴿Into a known measure﴾, which is the time of birth.
﴿So We determined﴾ upon that, ﴿and excellent are the Determiners﴾, We.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 77, verse 25:

﴿Kifātan﴾ is a verbal noun (maṣdar) of kafata, meaning "to gather together" (ḍamm), i.e., gathering together (ḍāmmah).

Translation:

﴿Living﴾ upon its surface, ﴿and dead﴾ within its belly.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 77, verse 27:

﴿And We placed therein firm mountains, lofty⦆ mountains, high ones, ﴿and We gave you to drink sweet water﴾ fresh, sweet water.

Note: the Qur'anic quotations above should be marked with ﴿ ﴾ and the glosses are the commentary's words.
Woe on that Day to those who deny! (28) And it is said to the deniers on the Day of Resurrection:
﴿Proceed to that which you used to deny﴾ of the punishment.
﴿Depart to a shadow of three branches﴾ It is the smoke of Jahannam (Hell). When it rises, it splits into three columns because of its enormity.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 77, verse 31:

﴿Nor any shade﴾ (ظَلِيل, zalil) a shelter that would shade them from the heat of that Day. ﴿Nor will it avail﴾ it will not ward off from them anything ﴿against the blaze﴾ (اللَّهَب, al-lahab), the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 77, verse 32:

﴿Indeed it﴾ — i.e., the Fire — ﴿throws up sparks﴾ — the sparks being what flies off from it — ﴿like a palace﴾ — of building — in its immensity and height.

Verse 77:33: ﴿As if they were yellow camels﴾ "Jimalat" is the plural of "jamal" (camel), and in another reading it is "jimalat" (with a different vowelling). ﴿Yellow (ṣufr)﴾ refers to their form and their colour. In a hadith: "The worst of people are black like pitch (al-qir)." The Arabs call black camels "ṣufr" because their blackness is mixed with yellowness, so some say ṣufr in the verse means black, for the reason mentioned; and others say no. "Al-sharar" is the plural of "shararah" (spark), and "al-qir" is pitch (al-qar).

This is the Day of Judgment, the day when they will not speak (lit. "they do not speak") in it at all.

Note: Surah 77, verse 35 reads: "This is a day they will not speak."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 77, verse 36:

﴿And they will not be permitted﴾ to present an excuse, ﴿so they will not make excuses﴾. It is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to "they will be permitted" without being a consequence of it; thus it falls within the scope of negation, meaning: there is no permission, so there is no excuse-making.
This is the day of decision; We have gathered you, O deniers of this nation, and the earlier ones (of the deniers before you), so that you may be judged and punished, all together.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 77, verse 39:

﴿If you have any stratagem﴾, a scheme for averting the punishment from you, ﴿then use your stratagem against Me﴾, so do it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 77, verse 41:

﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in shades﴾ i.e., dense clusters of trees, since there will be no sun to shade them from its heat, ﴿and springs﴾ gushing forth with water.

Translation of the passage:

﴿And fruits of whatever they desire.﴾ This informs that food and drink in Paradise are according to their desires, unlike in this world, where they are according to what people generally find. And it is said to them:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 77, verse 43:

﴿Eat and drink with wholesome enjoyment﴾ (hanīʾan), a circumstantial clause, meaning: enjoying it without any harm, ﴿for what you used to do﴾ of obedience.
[Quranic verse] ﴿Indeed, We thus﴾ as We rewarded the righteous.

ÔÇªThe passage is short; translating faithfully:

﴿Eat and enjoy yourselves﴾ is an address to the disbelievers in this world, ﴿for a little while﴾ of time, its limit being death. And in this there is a threat to them.

And when it is said to them, "Bow down [in prayer]" (ارْكَعُوا, irkaʿū), [they] pray (ṣallū)... they do not bow down (لا يَرْكَعُونَ, lā yarkaʿūna), [meaning] they do not pray (لا يُصَلُّونَ, lā yuṣallūna).

Note on the translation: the passage contains no further gloss, and I have kept the text as given. I added the transliterations of the Arabic words, which the instructions require for technical terms on first appearance, and the bracketed "[in prayer]" and "[they]" are the translator's supplements to make the Arabic-verb glosses readable in English.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 77, verse 50:

﴿So in what discourse after this will they believe?﴾ That is, the Qur'an. ﴿Will they believe?﴾ That is, it is impossible for them to believe in any other of God's books after their denial of it, because it contains the inimitability (i'jaz) which no other [book] contains.
